 Wed 18 Nov 2026 , Men's One Day International Series - 3rd ODI Australia (batting) vs England, in play Australia Australia In Play England England 114 -4 ( 26.0 ) 328 all out ( 48.3 ) Australia need 215 runs to win from 24.0 overs with 6 wickets remaining Australia innings: 114 for 4 from 26.0 overs, in play
 England innings: 328 all out from 48.3 overs
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 Bancroft says whole Australia team knew about sandpapergate 
 Australia slip to 34-3 in chase of 329 to win series
 Duckett, dropped on 29, hits century for England 
 Root , Cox & Duckett fall to impressive Renshaw (3-51)
 Archer holes out after being promoted to six 
 Try our interval quiz 
 Close form Have your say on England men this winter

 by Ffion Wynne
 Aus 113-4 published at 25 overs 25 overs 
 Four runs off Gus Atkinson's over, a two and a pair of singles - Australia haven't scored a boundary for 37 balls now.
 We reach the halfway mark with England in control - they were 157-3 at this stage.
 Here's Ffion Wynne to take you through the rest of the innings.

 Wow. Cummins and co must be in big trouble now. Had they just owned up after the Khawaja allegations, I think this would’ve blown over. But the decision to play defence could genuinely cost him the captaincy.

 Michael Vaughan 
Former England captain on Test Match Special 
 Pat Cummins pretty much denied
everything that Cam Bancroft has come out and said. Now, the one thing that
Cummins did say is that he had no knowledge of sandpaper being used on that
given day in Cape Town.
 I actually thought to myself, I can believe that. But
now I have read Cameron’s story, and he is saying that it was being used
before, I think many around the world always realised that there is no way in a
million years that the rest of the team wouldn’t have known.

 Aus 108-3 published at 23 overs 23 overs 
 Woops, and again Harry.
 The England skipper contrives to fling the ball out of his hand trying to collect Alex Carey's drive into the covers.
 The batters run two, meanwhile Brook heads off the field at the end of the over - he maybe needs someone to look at a finger or two.

 Renshaw dropped on 55 published at 22.3 overs 22.3 overs 
 Aus 106-3 
 Image source, Getty Images Matt Renshaw is dropped for a second time!
 Having already been dropped on six, the Australia number three is spilled by Harry Brook this time.
 It's a big toe-end up in the air off Gus Atkinson and Brook runs out into the extra cover region from mid-off, seemingly setting himself but letting the ball bounce out of his hands.
 Renshaw takes a single to move to 56.

 This is Australia's first 50-plus partnership for the fourth wicket in an ODI at home against England since 2018. The last such stand was a 68-run partnership between Steve Smith and Mitchell Marsh.

 Aus 105-3 published at 22 overs 22 overs 
 Four singles and a wide off Jofra Archer's fifth over - he's 0-25 thus far.
 Meanwhile the required run-rate has hit exactly eight runs an over.
 26 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Bancroft speaks on sandpapergate and says 'whole team' knew published at 09:06 GMT 09:06 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images There has been another big twist in the Sandpaper saga.
 In an explosive article in The West Australian newspaper, , external Cameron Bancroft has said he lied to Cricket Australia's initial investigation and has backed Usman Khawaja's claim that the whole team knew about the ball-tampering.
 He says he used sandpaper on the ball in the Port Elizabeth Test as well as Cape Town and he had conversations with the bowlers "about whether it was reverse swinging enough".
 He said Pat Cummins' press conference last week in which he said did not know sandpaper was being used made him feel "angry, betrayed and alone".
 "It was not just the three of us — Steve Smith, David Warner and I — who knew about me using sandpaper on the ball in South Africa," Bancroft said.
 "It was the whole team."
